claimReview: Creator production assertions, observed sampled frames, model-specific mathematical results and perceptual hypotheses retain separate evidentiary roles.

normalization.title: What a Swarm Makes Us See
normalization.overview: HORTRAME's audiovisual swarm film turns computed-looking formations into an immersive story; a sparse visual capture and source papers support a careful separation of image, mathematical model and viewer inference.
normalization.whyItMatters: Simulated coordination can be visually persuasive even when its implementation, operational failure cases and perceptual effects remain unmeasured.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Keep the artwork's wonder while tracing any operational claim back to versioned state rules, source coverage and a test that can fail.
normalization.falsification: Revisit the separation if a pinned render and code trace prove the advertised model and matched tests establish behavior under changing membership, realistic delay and recovery; evaluate perceptual effects only in a consented film-specific study.
normalization.freshness: Original YouTube page, six author-deposited Zenodo records and cited primary research checked October 22, 2026. Private visual inspection sampled 86 frames every twenty seconds and four ending frames; audio, continuous motion and film-specific viewer effects were not inspected.

claims.proposition: The inspected samples show point fields, repeated multi-lobed forms, rows, concentric arrangements, a dotted wireframe and a final bright-rimmed circle.
claims.assessment: A hash-bound private map describes 86 frames spaced twenty seconds apart and four ending checks.
claims.limits: This is sparse sampled visual coverage, not a continuous shot or motion trace; counts and scene boundaries are approximate.

claims.proposition: HORTRAME says the film uses thousands of simulated drones and computed priority-state, formation and light dynamics.
claims.assessment: The description states the method, and the visual field is compatible with simulation, but the render-to-code binding was not audited.
claims.limits: A film cannot expose exact agent count, update equations, parameter values or code provenance by appearance alone.

claims.proposition: Bolduc v07 characterizes a prescribed join-mix-depart endpoint and rejects unrestricted preservation of the original population mean.
claims.assessment: The author-deposited manuscript states assumptions, an offline formula and a counterexample; its scope can be checked in the public text.
claims.limits: GhostMesh did not independently certify every proof, reproduce the code, or show that the film uses the proved model.

claims.proposition: The cited delay analysis concerns fixed membership and does not establish a combined delayed, changing-membership film implementation.
claims.assessment: The arXiv delay abstract and Bolduc v07 scope statements keep these model obligations separate.
claims.limits: This is a documentary scope finding, not a negative test of HORTRAME's software or an assertion that no implementation could exist.

claims.proposition: The bright-rimmed dark circle and circular point field are visual motifs, not evidence of a physical singularity or robotic rendezvous.
claims.assessment: The sampled private frames show the motif, and the creator calls the cosmic setting artistic.
claims.limits: The gaps between stills do not establish continuous trajectories or the mechanism behind the rendering.

claims.proposition: The creator says pulse-coupled oscillators inform the light rhythm and a signal-processing project informs the score.
claims.assessment: Mirollo and Strogatz's idealized model exists, but no film-specific timing or audio analysis was performed.
claims.limits: Audio was uninspected; no soundtrack synchronization, entrainment or viewer effect is established.
claims.sourceLocation: Creator description; no verified soundtrack timestamp

claims.proposition: Optic-flow and viewpoint cues could contribute to visual self-motion impressions for some viewers, without establishing this film's effect.
claims.assessment: Independent visual-display studies support vection under studied stimuli; a separate VR experiment limits any broad beat-alignment story.
claims.limits: No viewer study of this film, display-condition control, medical outcome or hypnosis measure exists in this Reader.
claims.sourceLocation: 28:00 sampled frame and separate perceptual literature

claims.proposition: HORTRAME says the film's image, video and music were computationally produced without generative AI image, video or music models.
claims.assessment: The creator distinguishes procedural simulation and algorithmic score from generative AI tooling.
claims.limits: No project files, render pipeline or model-use audit was obtained; procedural generation is still a form of computation.

relationships.reason: Both Readers question the jump from an agent simulation or observed behavior to a broader story about system capability. The earlier Reader concerns reward pressure and reported agent play, while this one concerns a visual swarm artwork; their sources do not corroborate each other.

normalization.relationshipDisposition: One qualified thematic route to a different simulation-evidence critique. Similar words such as singularity or swarm do not establish a shared claim or corroboration.

relationshipReview.rationale: Compared the film's visual and mathematical thesis with all 32 current Readers. This one route clarifies simulation-evidence limits without treating unrelated videos, agent fleets or singularity forecasts as independent corroboration. The pinned DeepInfer repository addresses inference serving, not the film’s sampled visual swarm or its cited mathematics; no new outgoing route is supported. The new Hassabis profile was compared for a specific shared claim; no further typed relation is admitted on thematic overlap alone. The Orca fleet Reader was compared as a newer neighbor; its three outbound routes cover the supported comparisons, without reciprocal corroboration. The newly added LangChain webhook Reader was compared for a distinct source-grounded relationship; no existing typed edge is changed by this candidate.
